title: perf(canary): adaptive regression detection + rollout guards (KV hysteresis, throughput SLOs)
author: Aditi Kapoor
description:
Motivation: our current perf canary detects latency regressions via static thresholds which causes noisy rollouts for workloads with bursty traffic and KV-cache warmups. This change adds adaptive regression detection with hysteresis for KV-cache effects and throughput-aware SLOs, plus rollout guard rules to prevent unsafe automatic promotions.

Summary of changes: updated detector algorithms to use moving-window baselines and exponential smoothing, added KV-warmup hysteresis to avoid false positives during cache re-population, introduced throughput SLO checking (requests/sec) as a gating signal for rollouts, and added a rollback policy that triggers on sustained error/latency regressions. Also adds end-to-end integration tests and docs for configuration.

What this PR includes (high level):
- algorithm: adaptive_detector.go + tests
- rollout guards: rollout_guard_controller.go, policies DSL updates
- KV hysteresis: kv_warmup_tracker.go (new), metrics mappings
- SLO integration: canary_slo_evaluator.go (checks latency + throughput + error rate)
- API: canary admin endpoint to "dry-run" decisions and fetch evaluation traces
- telemetry: new Prometheus metrics and tracing tags to explain decisions
- docs: docs/perf-canary/configuration.md and release notes

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for detector logic
- [x] Integration tests simulating KV warmup and throughput spikes
- [x] Benchmarked on perf lab (latency detection false positive rate down ~72%)
- [x] Docs and release notes
- [x] Feature flagged behind `perf_canary_adaptive`

Rollout plan: feature-flag on for internal canaries for 2 weeks, collect false-positive and rollback events, then enable for canaries behind canary-tier=beta. If regression rate >1% or any critical rollback, auto-disable and notify SRE.

Notes: configuration defaults are conservative; operators can tune sensitivity and hysteresis windows. Related work: ENG-3271 (adaptive canary detector), ENG-3334 (rollout guard DSL), SUP-412 (incident follow-up: noisy canary during KV migration).
